1.explanation:
• src/ol/source/TileDebug.js: This is where the library actually draws the red grid tiles and labels their Z/X/Y indices. It currently just takes the raw tileCoord[2] (y) and renders it, without applying any inversion logic. That is exactly where you would inject the same “invert y” calculation that tileurlfunction.js does for a {-y} placeholder.  

• src/ol/tileurlfunction.js: This module implements the parsing of URL templates, including support for the special “{-y}” placeholder. When you change TileDebug to mirror its behavior you can call into this code (or borrow its inversion formula) so that the debug layer shows exactly the same Y values that the URL templating engine sends.  

• src/ol/source/UrlTile.js: This base class wires up tileUrlFunction (and the underlying getTileCoordForTileUrl routine) to UrlTile-derived sources. XYZ and TileImage both inherit this logic. Reviewing it shows how UrlTile builds its final request coordinates; TileDebug should do the same when it is asked to infer the inverted Y.  

• src/ol/source/XYZ.js: This convenience subclass sets up the default XYZ tile grid (including its origin/top-left orientation) and delegates to UrlTile for templating. It’s where {-y} is expected to flip against the grid’s origin. TileDebug can either switch to using the same tileGrid instance or at least re-use its invert-Y math so that both layers report the same coordinates.
1.bug_scenario: When you turn on the built-in TileDebug overlay against a TileImage (XYZ) layer whose URL template uses the “{-y}” placeholder, the little red debug tiles still label themselves with the raw y index (0,1,2…) instead of the inverted index that the server actually receives. In other words, the network requests are going out to e.g. /{z}/{x}/{-y}.png (so y=3→inverted to 4–3–1=0), but the TileDebug layer is drawing “Y: 3” rather than “Y: 0,” so your debug grid and your real tiles don’t line up.

2.explanation: TileDebug.js is the only source in the repository that draws debug tiles (with x/y/z labels) rather than fetching them via URL templates. All UrlTile derivatives (e.g. TileImage, XYZ) call getTileCoordForTileUrl internally, which applies the tileGrid logic for {y} vs. {-y} placeholders (using the generic tileurlfunction module). TileDebug, however, takes the raw tileCoord from the map and draws it directly, so it never applies the “invert Y” logic. To correct the discrepancy you must modify TileDebug.js so that it first calls this.getTileCoordForTileUrl(tileCoord) (inherited from UrlTile) and then uses the resulting coord when rendering — thereby honoring any {-y} inversion just like the real tile sources do.
2.bug_scenario: When using a TileDebug layer alongside an XYZ/TileImage layer whose URL template uses “{-y}” to flip the tile Y coordinate, the debug overlay still draws the raw Y it receives (uncorrected), while the image layer actually requests tiles with an inverted Y. You end up with mismatched tile indices: the debug grid shows one set of Y coordinates but the loaded PNG images come from a flipped Y scheme.
